Screening_and_Diuretics.Screening: Screening for and treatment of aetiologies, and CV and non-CV comorbidities is recommended in patients with HFpEF.
Screening_and_Diuretics.Diuretics: Diuretics are recommended in congested patients with HFpEF to alleviate symptoms and signs.

Prevention_of_chronic_HF.Hypertension: Treatment of hypertension is recommended to prevent or delay the onset of HF and to prevent HF hospitalizations.
Prevention_of_chronic_HF.Statins: Treatment with statins is recommended in patients at high risk of CV disease or with CV disease to prevent or delay onset of HF and to prevent HF hospitalizations.
Prevention_of_chronic_HF.SGLT2_inhibitors: SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with diabetes at high CV risk or with CV disease to prevent HF hospitalizations.
Prevention_of_chronic_HF.Lifestyle: Counselling against sedentary behaviour, obesity, cigarette smoking, and alcohol abuse is recommended to prevent or delay onset of HF.

Management_of_chronic_HF.Multidisciplinary_programmes: HF patients should be enrolled in multidisciplinary HF management programmes to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and mortality.
Management_of_chronic_HF.Self_management: Self-management strategies are recommended to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and mortality.
Management_of_chronic_HF.Home_or_clinic_programmes: Home-based and/or clinic-based programmes improve outcomes and are recommended to reduce HF hospitalization and mortality.
Management_of_chronic_HF.Exercise: Exercise is recommended for patients able to improve exercise capacity and quality of life and reduce HF hospitalization.

Advanced_HF.MCS_candidate_requirements: Patients considered for long-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) must have good compliance, capacity for device handling, and psychosocial support.
Advanced_HF.Heart_transplantation: Heart transplantation is recommended for patients with advanced HF refractory to medical/device therapy who do not have absolute contraindications.

Acute_HF.Oxygen: Oxygen is recommended when SpO2 <90% or PaO2 <60 mmHg to correct hypoxaemia.
Acute_HF.Intubation: Intubation is recommended for progressive respiratory failure despite oxygen or non-invasive ventilation.
Acute_HF.IV_loop_diuretics: Intravenous loop diuretics are recommended for all patients with acute HF with signs/symptoms of fluid overload to improve symptoms.
Acute_HF.Thromboprophylaxis: Thromboprophylaxis (e.g., LMWH) is recommended in patients not already anticoagulated and without contraindication to reduce risk of DVT and pulmonary embolism.
Acute_HF.Inotropes: Inotropic agents are not recommended routinely due to safety concerns, unless the patient has symptomatic hypotension and evidence of hypoperfusion.
Acute_HF.Opioids: Routine use of opioids is not recommended, except in selected patients with severe/intractable pain or anxiety.
Acute_HF.IABP: Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is not routinely recommended in post-MI cardiogenic shock.

Post_hospitalization_management.Evaluation_before_discharge: Patients hospitalized for HF should be carefully evaluated to exclude persistent signs of congestion before discharge and to optimize oral treatment.
Post_hospitalization_management.Administer_evidence_based_treatment: Recommended evidence-based oral medical treatment should be administered before discharge when possible.
Post_hospitalization_management.Early_follow_up: An early follow-up visit (1–2 weeks after discharge) is recommended to assess signs of congestion, drug tolerance, and to start/continue uptitration of therapy.

HF_and_AF.Anticoagulation: Long-term oral anticoagulation is recommended in patients with AF, HF, and CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥2 in men or ≥3 in women.
HF_and_AF.DOACs_vs_VKAs: DOACs are recommended in preference to VKAs for patients with HF, except in those with moderate/severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic valves.
HF_and_AF.Urgent_ECV: Urgent electrical cardioversion (ECV) is recommended in acute worsening of HF with rapid ventricular rates and haemodynamic instability.
HF_and_AF.Antiarrhythmic_safety: Certain anti-arrhythmic agents (flecainide, encainide, disopyramide, dronedarone, and D-sotalol) are not recommended due to safety concerns.
